items.title: 川普啟動產能過剩關稅：日本抗議、巴西反嗆「不合法、將對等回擊」
items.title_en: Trump Launches Overcapacity Tariffs: Japan Protests, Brazil Retorts "Illegal, Will Retaliate in Kind"
paras: 美國貿易代表辦公室(USTR)周三(25日)宣布，擬對日本進口商品課徵15%關稅，並保留上調至20%空間；同時對巴西成品飛機加徵10%從價稅、對配額外原糖設新稅率，措施依據「產能過剩調查」與301條款，聲稱要倒逼貿易對手糾正非市場做法。
日本內閣官房長官木原稔周四(26日)明確否認「結構性產能過剩」指控，並稱「日本沒有任何非市場政策或做法，美方舉措令人遺憾。」
日本15%稅率落在去年與美國協議框架之內，東京承諾5500億美元對美投資計畫，換取美方將多數商品關稅天花板設在15%、汽車適用更低稅率；協議並載明若東京當局投資不到位，華府可加稅。雖然美國最高法院今年2月裁定川普全球關稅無效後，多數日貨稅率曾降至12.5%，但日方仍咬牙履約。
目前，日本已分三輪公布投資案、總額1300億美元，推進速度快於南韓等同類協議方，日本經濟產業大臣赤澤亮正此前承諾「忠實落實就不會破15%」，木原稔也強調投資穩步執行。抗議歸抗議，東京選擇用資本換關稅緩衝。
巴西反應則更強硬。巴西外交部譴責USTR「單方面決定不可接受」，指出8月21日巴西總統魯拉跟川普通话後雙方同意設工作組，但美方遲未提交協定框架，談判自9月停滯；新關稅實為施壓巴西修改Pix支付、數位貿易與優惠協定等國內監管。
USTR代表格里爾表示，巴西「一年談判無實質進展」，巴西反斥美方藉飛機、糖兩大支柱產業開刀，並強調「不向威脅低頭」，同時尋求多元市場分散風險。
同樣被加稅，日本用「投資換穩定」，巴西用「規則戰＋對等威脅」。華爾街更在意前者：汽車與半導體供應鏈關稅不失控，是亞洲風險資產的底，後者則把農產、民航與數位主權扯進2027選舉週期。川普的關稅工具箱從「緊急狀態」轉回301條款，法律更穩、談判更狠，全球貿易折現率再度上修。
paras_en: The U.S. Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR) announced on Wednesday (the 25th) that it plans to impose a 15% tariff on Japanese imports, with the possibility of raising it to 20%; at the same time it will add a 10% ad‑valorem duty on finished aircraft from Brazil and set a new rate for extra‑quota raw sugar. The measures are based on an “overcapacity investigation” and Section 301, and are said to be intended to force trading partners to correct non‑market practices.

Japan’s Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara on Thursday (the 26th) flatly denied the allegation of “structural overcapacity,” stating that “Japan has no non‑market policies or practices, and the U.S. action is regrettable.”

The 15% Japanese rate falls within the framework of last year’s agreement with the United States, under which Tokyo pledged a $550 billion investment plan in the U.S. in exchange for the U.S. capping most tariffs at 15% and applying a lower rate to automobiles. The agreement also stipulates that if Tokyo fails to meet its investment commitments, Washington can raise the duties. Although the U.S. Supreme Court ruled in February that Trump’s global tariffs were invalid, most Japanese‑made goods saw rates fall to 12.5%, Japan has nonetheless pressed ahead with its commitments.

To date Japan has announced three rounds of investment projects totaling $130 billion, moving faster than South Korea and other counterparties. Japan’s Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry Ryosuke Akazawa previously pledged to “faithfully implement it so the 15% ceiling will not be broken,” and Kihara emphasized that the investments are being carried out steadily. In short, Tokyo is using capital to offset the tariff pressure.

Brazil’s response is far tougher. Brazil’s foreign ministry condemned the USTR’s “unilateral decision as unacceptable,” noting that on August 21 President Lula and Trump agreed to set up a working group, but the U.S. has yet to submit a framework, and negotiations have stalled since September. The new tariffs are seen as pressure on Brazil to change its Pix payment system, digital trade rules and preferential‑trade agreements.

USTR representative Gillian (Grill) said Brazil has seen “a year of negotiations with no substantive progress,” accusing Brazil of using its two flagship sectors—aircraft and sugar—to fight back, and stressing that “we will not bow to threats,” while Brazil is seeking to diversify markets to spread risk.

Both Japan and Brazil are hit by the new duties, but Japan is responding with “investment for stability,” whereas Brazil is using “rules‑based warfare and reciprocal threats.” Wall Street is more focused on the former: keeping auto and semiconductor supply‑chain tariffs in check is seen as the floor for Asian risk assets, while the latter drags agriculture, civil aviation and digital sovereignty into the 2027 election cycle. Trump’s tariff toolbox has shifted from an “emergency” basis back to Section 301, a more legally solid and tougher negotiating lever, pushing up the global trade discount rate again.

items.title: 日銀委員釋加快升息訊號 稱須迅速因應通膨風險
items.title_en: BoJ Official Signals Faster Rate Hikes, Says Prompt Action Needed on Inflation Risks
paras: 《路透社》報導，日本銀行(BoJ)審議委員田村直樹(Naoki Tamura)週四(26日)表示，央行必須迅速因應通膨超出預期的跡象，包括加快升息步調。
田村在一場演講中表示，「考量到金融情勢仍維持寬鬆，我認為日本銀行應盡快將政策利率調升至被認為對經濟中性的水準。」
田村指出，原物料成本上升，包括中東衝突推升原油價格，已導致批發通膨大幅攀升，價格壓力也逐漸擴散至各類消費產品。
他表示，受到中東局勢發展不確定性、日元走勢，以及AI相關商品需求依然強勁等因素影響，「近期物價變化顯示，通膨面臨進一步上行風險」。
田村指出，日本的通膨預期不像其他經濟體那樣穩固錨定，因此更有必要進一步升息。
他表示，金融情勢仍維持寬鬆，調查顯示，日本銀行過去的升息措施，以及未來可能進行的升息，不太可能對企業活動造成重大衝擊。
田村表示，「每次升息後的幾個月內，日銀便能根據企業訪談取得的資訊，以及各項調查結果，合理評估金融情勢。」
他指出，「日本的潛在消費者物價指數(CPI)通膨，尚未像其他經濟體一樣穩固錨定在央行2%的目標，因此我認為，央行必須迅速因應物價出現上行偏離目標的跡象，包括加快政策利率的升息步調。」
paras_en: Reuters reported that BoJ policy‑maker Naoki Tamura said on Thursday (the 26th) that the central bank must act quickly to inflation that is running hotter than expected, including accelerating the pace of rate hikes.

Tamura said in a speech that, given financial conditions remain accommodative, he believes the Bank of Japan should raise the policy rate to a level considered neutral for the economy as soon as possible.

He noted that rising commodity costs, including higher oil prices driven by Middle‑East conflict, have caused wholesale inflation to surge sharply, with price pressures spreading to a wide range of consumer goods.

Tamura added that recent price developments, amid uncertainty over the Middle‑East situation, the yen’s trajectory and still‑strong demand for AI‑related products, show inflation faces further upside risk.
He pointed out that Japan’s inflation expectations are not as firmly anchored as in other economies, making additional rate hikes even more necessary.
Tamura said that because financial conditions remain loose, surveys indicate that past BoJ rate hikes and any future hikes are unlikely to cause a major shock to corporate activity.
He explained that “in the months following each rate hike, the BoJ can reasonably assess financial conditions based on information gathered from corporate interviews and various surveys.”

He concluded that “Japan’s underlying CPI inflation has not yet become as firmly anchored at the 2% target as in other economies, so the central bank must respond swiftly to signs of price deviations upward, including speeding up the pace of policy‑rate hikes.”

items.title: 美啟動「產能過剩」301關稅：南韓暫守15%、中國20%　1月聽證定生死
items.title_en: U.S. Launches “Overcapacity” 301 Tariffs: South Korea Holds at 15%, China at 20% – Jan Hearing Will Decide Fate
paras: 美國貿易代表辦公室(USTR)週三(25日)公布《貿易法》第301條調查結果，指稱南韓、日本、中國、歐盟等14個經濟體透過產業補貼、政策金融與非市場經濟進口，製造「結構性產能過剩」，擬對相關商品加徵關稅，此舉顯示華府意在最高法院此前裁定對等關稅無效後，換一套法律外衣重建關稅壁壘，重新掌握單邊貿易制裁的主動權。
根據USTR提出的建議方案，擬對南韓、日本及歐盟商品課徵最高15%的關稅，對中國大陸擬課20%，但對川普第一任期內已被加徵約25%關稅的部分商品，此次20%將作為額外稅率疊加，且備案中最高稅率可達40%。不過，這並非最終實施稅率，USTR將在明年1月5日前接收書面意見，並於1月25日舉行公開聽證會，隨後才會敲定最終措施。
綜合《KBS》、《韓聯社》等韓媒報導，南韓此次暫時守住15%的關稅天花板，關鍵在於去年兩國達成的3500億美元對美投資協議及能源採購承諾。去年雙方商定將關稅上限設定在15%，此前市場普遍擔憂，南韓今年對美貿易順差大幅擴大，恐引發美方突破上限。
受AI投資熱潮推動，今年前10月南韓對美貿易順差1023億美元，史上首次突破千億美元大關，超過去年495億美元的兩倍，這一數據雖然支撐出口，但也讓華府更有籌碼施壓首爾對阿拉斯加液化天然氣(LNG)等對美投資項目的落實進度。
然而，USTR點名南韓汽車、半導體、石油化工等產業受國策銀行過度扶持，若後續磋商進展或投資履約情況未能令美方滿意，稅率可再拉升至25%。日本和歐盟的備案最高稅率則為20%，這意味著「15%」並非永久保險，而是一個動態的談判基線。
更敏感的火藥庫在「數位政策」領域。美方已將韓數位監管措施視為非關稅貿易壁壘，美國國會近期也釋出信號暗示，恐對數位貿易領域啟動新的301調查。這讓不確定性從傳統關稅表延伸到平台經濟、AI治理與跨境資料流規則，為韓美經貿關係埋下另一顆未爆彈。
市場分析師解讀這套「產能過剩關稅」有兩條主線：短期來看，主要盟友稅率「可控」避免了供應鏈即時斷鏈，但半導體、電池、汽車等關鍵出口成本仍將墊高，企業利潤率面臨壓縮；中長期而言，這套基於301條款的關稅比之前的IEEPA緊急狀態稅更耐法律訴訟，恐成為跨政府持續使用的貿易工具。
南韓貿易協會國際貿易通商研究院長張相植(音譯)表示，關稅不確定性有所降低，將有助於企業制定對美投資和出口計畫，但競爭環境隨時可能因談判結果而改變。
華爾街與首爾智庫的共識是：這不是單純的貿易罰單，而是「投資換關稅」的動態綁架機制。短期反彈看AI需求與供應鏈韌性，但企業底線須看華府的政治滿意度。
在1月聽證會結果出爐前，亞洲出口商仍需嚴陣以待，重新檢視原產地佈局與稅號清單，不能再將15%視為不可動搖的永久底線。
paras_en: The U.S. Trade Representative’s Office (USTR) announced on Wednesday (the 25th) the results of its Section 301 investigation under the Trade Act, accusing 14 economies—including South Korea, Japan, China and the EU—of creating “structural overcapacity” through industrial subsidies, policy financing and non‑market‑economy imports, and proposing tariffs on the affected goods. This move shows Washington’s intent to rebuild tariff barriers under a new legal guise after the Supreme Court ruled previous reciprocal tariffs ineffective, thereby regaining the initiative in unilateral trade sanctions.

According to the USTR’s proposed plan, tariffs of up to 15% would be levied on goods from South Korea, Japan and the EU, and 20% on goods from mainland China. For products that were already subject to roughly 25% tariffs during the first Trump administration, the new 20% would be added on top, with a maximum rate in the filing that could reach 40%. These are not final rates; the USTR will accept written comments by Jan. 5 2025 and hold a public hearing on Jan. 25, after which the final measures will be set.

South Korean media such as KBS and Yonhap reported that South Korea’s temporary hold on the 15% tariff ceiling hinges on a $350 billion investment and energy‑procurement pact signed with the United States last year. The two sides agreed to cap tariffs at 15%, easing market fears that South Korea’s sharply expanding trade surplus with the U.S. this year might trigger a breach of that limit.

Driven by the AI investment boom, South Korea’s trade surplus with the U.S. reached $102.3 billion in the first ten months of this year – the first time it has topped $100 billion, more than double the $49.5 billion surplus recorded last year. While this bolsters exports, it also gives Washington more leverage to press Seoul on the implementation of U.S.‑bound projects such as Alaskan LNG.

However, the USTR singled out South Korea’s auto, semiconductor and petrochemical sectors for excessive support from state‑owned banks. If subsequent negotiations or investment compliance fall short of U.S. expectations, the tariff rate could be raised to 25%. The filing lists a maximum of 20% for Japan and the EU, indicating that the “15%” figure is not a permanent guarantee but a dynamic negotiation baseline.

A more sensitive flashpoint lies in the “digital policy” arena. The U.S. has deemed South Korean digital regulation measures a non‑tariff trade barrier, and Congress has recently signaled the possibility of launching a new Section 301 probe in the digital trade space. This extends uncertainty from traditional tariffs to platform economics, AI governance and cross‑border data flow rules, planting another unexploded bomb in the Korea‑U.S. economic relationship.

Market analysts see two strands in this “overcapacity tariff” scheme: in the short term, keeping allied rates “controllable” avoids an immediate supply‑chain break, but key export costs in semiconductors, batteries and automobiles will still rise, squeezing corporate profit margins; in the medium‑to‑long term, a Section 301‑based tariff is more legally resilient than the emergency IEEPA taxes previously used, potentially becoming a lasting tool for inter‑governmental trade pressure.

Zhang Xiangzhi (phonetic), director of the International Trade and Commerce Research Institute at the Korea International Trade Association, said that reduced tariff uncertainty will help firms plan U.S. investments and export strategies, though the competitive environment could shift at any moment depending on negotiation outcomes.

The consensus among Wall Street analysts and Seoul think‑tanks is that this is not a simple trade fine but a dynamic “investment‑for‑tariff” hostage mechanism. Short‑term rebounds may come from AI demand and supply‑chain resilience, but corporate bottom lines will ultimately depend on Washington’s political satisfaction.

Until the January hearing’s outcome is known, Asian exporters must stay on high alert, reassess origin‑allocation strategies and tariff‑code listings, and can no longer treat the 15% rate as an immutable, permanent floor.

items.title: AI記憶體紅利推高經濟成長！南韓央行宣布升息1碼抗通膨 與美利差降至0.75個百分點
items.title_en: AI Memory Bonus Fuels Economic Growth! South Korea Central Bank Raises Interest Rate by 1 Basis Point to Combat Inflation, US-Korea Spread Drops to 0.75 Percentage Point
paras: 南韓央行(BOK)週四(26日)宣布將7天期回購利率上調25個基點至3.25%，結束10月暫停節奏、恢復升息。今年7、8月連升兩次後累計緊縮幅度達75個基點，這是BOK今年下半年第三次升息，與美國的利率差距縮至0.75個百分點。
BOK同步上修經濟成長預期，今年GDP成長率估值從3.3%調高至3.9%，2027年從2.9%上調至4.1%；10月消費者物價指數(CPI)仍達2.8%，核心通膨2.8%，均高於2%目標，房價也還在漲。
驅動力來自「出口端超強、消費端偏弱」的撕裂基本面。全球AI基礎建設投資帶動HBM與企業級NAND超級週期，南韓半導體出口放量，推升經濟成長遠超預期。
BOK決策官員釋放清晰信號：在半導體榮景抵銷家庭需求疲軟、韓股綜合股指(KOSPI)波動的當下，通膨壓力與出口驅動擴張優先級壓過內需擔憂。
不過，市場並非全無顧慮。美銀指出，經常帳順差撐住韓元，但外資持續拋售韓股、綜合指數難守5000點上方；高盛則警告超額利潤集中在三星、海力士兩家，未有效外溢到居民部門，消費僅溫和復甦。
BOK總裁申鉉松隨後記者會成焦點，市場將觀察「終端利率是否衝3.5%」與2027年經濟成長預期會否再上修。若明年GDP成長率估值破3.5%，代表央行對半導體週期更樂觀、緊縮尾巴更長；若措辭轉鴿，則暗示內需與科技股財富效應萎縮已進入決策權衡。
paras_en: The Bank of Korea (BOK) announced on Thursday (26th) that it would raise the 7‑day repo rate by 25 basis points to 3.25%, ending the pause in October and resuming rate hikes. After two consecutive increases in July and August, the cumulative tightening has reached 75 basis points, marking the third rate hike for BOK in the second half of the year, and narrowing the gap with U.S. rates to 0.75 percentage point.

BOK also lifted its economic growth outlook, raising the estimated GDP growth rate for this year from 3.3% to 3.9% and for 2027 from 2.9% to 4.1%. The October consumer price index (CPI) remains at 2.8%, core inflation at 2.8%, both above the 2% target, and housing prices continue to rise.

The driving force comes from a split fundamental: a strong export side versus a weaker consumption side. Global AI infrastructure investment is driving a super‑cycle for HBM and enterprise‑grade NAND, boosting South Korean semiconductor exports and pushing economic growth far beyond expectations.

BOK decision makers sent a clear signal: amid the semiconductor boom offsetting weak household demand and volatility in the KOSPI, inflationary pressure and export‑driven expansion take priority over concerns about domestic demand.

However, the market is not without concerns. Bank of America noted that the current account surplus supports the won, but foreign investors continue to sell Korean stocks, making it difficult for the KOSPI to stay above 5,000 points. Goldman Sachs warned that excess profits are concentrated in Samsung and SK Hynix, not effectively spilling over to the consumer sector, and consumption is only mildly recovering.

BOK Governor Seon Hyeon‑song became the focus of a subsequent press conference, with the market watching whether the “terminal rate will hit 3.5%” and whether the 2027 growth outlook will be revised upward. If next year’s GDP growth estimate exceeds 3.5%, it would indicate the central bank is more optimistic about the semiconductor cycle and will keep tightening longer; a dovish tone would suggest that the contraction of domestic demand and the wealth effect of tech stocks have entered decision‑making considerations.

items.title: AI信仰遭遇極限壓力測試！美股超級「V轉」 分析師：深V不是轉折  是分歧
items.title_en: AI Faith Faces Extreme Pressure Test! US Stocks Super “V-Shape” Analysts: Deep V Is Not a Turning Point but a Divergence
paras: 華爾街週三(25日)上演一場「驚魂深V」劇本，盤中恐慌式殺盤，尾盤硬拉收回，但市場情緒的底層邏輯已經換了。
那斯達克100指數(NDX) 開盤5分鐘便重挫近5%，那斯達克指數一度跌約4.5%，標普500盤中跌超3%、道瓊指數(DJI) 一度狂瀉逾1100點，費城半導體(SOX)跌近8%，輝達(NVDA-US) 盤中一度跌近9%，隨後跌幅全數收斂，道瓊翻紅收漲0.33%，標普僅跌0.25%，那指收跌0.62%。
金銀同步演「超級V」，現貨金價盤中最低見到每盎司3426美元，尾盤拉回漲0.92%收3588.41美元，白銀盤中跌超6%，收漲1.15%至41.38美元。
兩天前白宮推動黃仁勳復任輝達執行長，曾讓AI鏈單日暴漲、那指漲超6%，但這波「情緒紓困」沒撐過一日遊。
Running Oak Capital執行長Seth Cogswell直言：「這試圖成為一次AI行業紓困，但沒奏效，人們看穿了。」
更麻煩的是治理溢價被撕開。標普全球評級週三將輝達AA評級列入「負面觀察」，指黃仁勳離任又復職暴露董事會獨立性、接班計畫與監督機制漏洞，90天內可能降至AA-，輝達週三收跌3.91%，CDS違約保護成本創新高。
真正壓抑風險偏好的，是敘事切換。Solstein Capital執行長Terman說：「市場不再爭論AI會不會改變世界，而在問誰能賺錢、能賺多少、數兆美元資本開支能不能回收。諷刺的是，技術承諾兌現了，財務回報卻可能讓投資人失望。」
聯準會(Fed)重啟緊縮讓這道題更尖銳：融資成本抬升，資料中心、HBM、算力租賃的ROI必須更高才合理。期中選舉後民主黨對資料中心擴張的阻力、出口管制不確定性，再疊一層政策折現風險。
NYSE交易廳老將Jonathan Corpina把當前市場情緒跟2008年時類比說道：「不是拋售規模一樣，是那種『接下來還會怎樣』的持續不安。」
TradeMas交易員Peter Tuchman則說：「從未見過同一個故事——英偉達——讓市場看法反轉得這麼徹底。」
分析師指出，拋售「有序」，獲利與宏觀底子還在，但盤面已變成情緒博弈。
Siebert Financial投資長Mark Malek苦笑說：「過去10天搖頭次數太多，脖子都酸了。」他客戶最怕的不是繼續跌，而是「萬一反彈踏空」。
深V不是轉折，是分歧。AI技術前景不再是最大爭議，「數兆美元投入能否變成足夠獲利、市場還願不願續費」才是定價核心。短期看Fed態度與輝達治理修補，中期看雲廠資本開支回報，這一輪洗盤後，留下的只會是最有信念、也最會算帳的資金。
paras_en: Wall Street staged a “deep V” drama on Wednesday (25th), with panic selling in the middle of the day and a hard pullback at the close, but the underlying market logic had already shifted.

The Nasdaq 100 (NDX) fell nearly 5% in the first five minutes of trading, the Nasdaq index briefly dropped about 4.5%, the S&P 500 fell over 3% mid‑day, the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJI) plunged more than 1,100 points, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) fell nearly 8%, and Nvidia (NVDA‑US) dropped almost 9% mid‑day before the declines converged; the Dow ended up 0.33% higher, the S&P only down 0.25%, and the Nasdaq down 0.62%.

Gold and silver both performed a “super V,” with spot gold hitting a low of $3,426 per ounce mid‑day and rebounding 0.92% to close at $3,588.41, while silver fell over 6% mid‑day and closed up 1.15% at $41.38.

Two days ago the White House pushed for Jensen Huang’s reappointment as Nvidia CEO, which once caused a one‑day surge in AI stocks and a 6% rise in the Nasdaq, but this “emotional relief” did not last beyond the day.
Running Oak Capital CEO Seth Cogswell bluntly said, “This was an attempt to provide a bailout for the AI industry, but it failed; people see through it.”

Complicating matters further, governance premiums were ripped apart. S&P Global Ratings placed Nvidia’s AA rating under “negative watch” on Wednesday, citing that Huang’s departure and return exposed board independence, succession planning, and oversight mechanism weaknesses, with a possible downgrade to AA‑ within 90 days. Nvidia fell 3.91% on Wednesday and CDS default protection costs hit a new high.

The real risk‑aversion comes from a narrative shift. Solstein Capital CEO Terman said, “The market no longer debates whether AI will change the world; it asks who can make money, how much, and whether the trillions of dollars in capital spend can be recouped. Ironically, the technology promise has been fulfilled, but financial returns may disappoint investors.”

The Fed’s re‑tightening makes this issue sharper: financing costs rise, and the ROI for data centers, HBM, and compute‑as‑a‑service must be higher to be justified. After the midterm election, Democratic resistance to data‑center expansion, export‑control uncertainty, and additional policy discount risk stack on.
NYSE veteran Jonathan Corpina compared the current market sentiment to 2008, saying, “It’s not the same scale of selling, but the persistent unease about ‘what will happen next’.”
TradeMas trader Peter Tuchman said, “I’ve never seen the same story—Nvidia—flip market sentiment so thoroughly.”
Analysts noted that the sell‑off is “ordered,” profits and macro fundamentals remain, but the market has become an emotional game.

Siebert Financial CIO Mark Malek grimaced, “We’ve been shaking our heads too many times in the past 10 days; our necks are sore.” He said his clients fear not a continued decline but a missed rebound if they sell too early.

The deep V is not a turning point but a divergence. The future of AI technology is no longer the biggest debate; the question is whether trillions of dollars of investment can generate sufficient profit and whether the market will continue to pay for it. In the short term, Fed stance and Nvidia governance fixes matter; in the midterm, cloud‑provider capital‑spend returns will determine the outcome. After this round of market cleaning, only the most committed and financially savvy investors will remain.

paras_en: The dollar weakened on Wednesday (the 25th), as AI‑related stocks plunged sharply before later recouping most of their early‑session losses, leaving the market highly volatile and pushing safe‑haven currencies the Swiss franc and the yen higher.

The Nasdaq Composite, which has a high weighting of technology stocks, fell about 4% at one point as AI‑theme shares came under renewed selling pressure, then rebounded, ending the session with a modest decline of roughly 0.6%.
The dollar had earlier benefited from rising market safe‑haven sentiment but turned lower in the latter part of the trading session.
In the New York close, the U.S. Dollar Index (DXY), which tracks the dollar against six major currencies, slipped 0.22% to 103.62.

InvestingLive chief FX analyst Adam Button said the equity market saw a “large counter‑attack.” “I wonder whether this is merely a short‑covering rally caused by the shortened trading week due to the holiday, but even in the worst case it at least signals that the market is regaining some vigor,” he added.
Most U.S. markets will be closed on Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday.
In past market sell‑offs the dollar has acted as a safe‑haven currency, yet it is also influenced by capital flows tied to the AI investment boom and expectations for economic growth.
The euro rose 0.17% against the dollar to $1.0983.
The yen gained 0.06% versus the dollar, trading at 159.13 yen per $1.
The dollar fell 0.63% against the Swiss franc, to 0.83 franc.
The risk‑sensitive Australian dollar slipped 0.15% to $0.6628, after briefly touching $0.6557 earlier, its lowest level since December 3.
Traders are also assessing that the Federal Reserve, still facing inflation above its target, may raise rates a few more times.

U.S. October inflation further accelerated, with the personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index up 0.3% month‑over‑month, after a 0.5% rise in September. Excluding the more volatile food and energy components, the core PCE price index also rose 0.3% last month, matching September’s unadjusted 0.3% gain.
However, with recent declines in oil prices, market inflation expectations have retreated over the past few weeks.

CIBC Capital Markets head of FX strategy Sarah Ying said, “The more important question is what level you think the ultimate interest rate will settle at. That’s why you see the 5‑year bond performing slightly better than the 2‑year, because most of the uncertainty is concentrated in the longer end rather than the near‑term foreseeable future.”

The yield curve between U.S. 2‑year and 5‑year Treasury bonds has flattened, with the spread now about 2 basis points, compared with a peak of 27 basis points last month. Market expectations of further Fed hikes are putting pressure on the rate‑sensitive 2‑year yields.

On the other hand, markets gave little reaction to the Trump administration’s Wednesday proposal to impose new tariffs on goods from 14 major trading partners. The tariffs are intended to address what the U.S. calls structural overcapacity in industry, with China facing the highest rates. Washington argues that China is the primary source of low‑priced exports that flood global markets. China has rejected the accusation, saying its exports reflect its own competitive advantages.

U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told CNBC on Wednesday that the proposed new tariffs would largely maintain the rates set under existing trade agreements, with some duties possibly rising a few percentage points.
Ying noted that the market had already priced in these tariff measures, so they did not move markets. “This is not a second ‘Liberation Day.’”
Elsewhere, Eurozone policy‑maker Olaf Sleijpen said on Tuesday that the European Central Bank may raise its policy rate in December, but the subsequent rate path remains unclear.

Bank of England governor Andrew Bailey said that if international energy prices stay at current levels after recent declines, UK inflation may not be as high as earlier this month’s forecasts suggested.

In Japan, official data showed that the key service‑sector inflation gauge rose 4.2% year‑over‑year in October, indicating expanding price pressure and further supporting the Bank of Japan’s recent rate‑hike rationale.
